+    solution_name = func_args[0].strip()
+    solution_params = re.findall(r'"([^"]*)"', func_args[1])

   186	  syntax KItem  ::= #evalArgs(Exprs, Vals, ApplyK)
   187	                  | #evalArgCont(Exprs, Vals, ApplyK)
   188	                  | #applyK(ApplyK, Vals)
   189	  rule <k> #evalArgs((A:Expr, REST:Exprs), ACC:Vals, K:ApplyK) => A ~> #evalArgCont(REST, ACC, K) ... </k>
   190	  rule <k> V:Val ~> #evalArgCont(REST:Exprs, ACC:Vals, K:ApplyK) => #evalArgs(REST, appendVal(ACC, V), K) ... </k>
   191	  rule <k> #evalArgs(.Exprs, ACC:Vals, K:ApplyK) => #applyK(K, ACC) ... </k>
   192	
   193	  // ==== Int / Bool / None literals ==========================================
   194	  rule <k> Int(I:Int)   => I ... </k>
   195	  rule <k> Bool(B:Bool) => B ... </k>
   196	  rule <k> NoneVal      => noneV ... </k>
   197	
   198	  // ==== truthy (If, Assert, BoolOp, IfExp, not, While) ======================
   199	  syntax Bool ::= truthy(Val) [function]
   200	  rule truthy(B:Bool)          => B
   201	  rule truthy(noneV)           => false
   202	  rule truthy(I:Int)           => I =/=Int 0
   203	  rule truthy(str(S:IntSeq))   => notBool (S ==K .IntSeq)
   204	  rule truthy(list(V:ValSeq))  => notBool (V ==K .ValSeq)
   205	  rule truthy(tuple(V:ValSeq)) => notBool (V ==K .ValSeq)
   206	
   207	  // ==== extensible operator dispatch (cases added by the construct modules) ==
   208	  syntax Val  ::= applyUn(String, Val) [function]
   209	  syntax Val  ::= applyBin(String, Val, Val) [function]
   210	  syntax Bool ::= applyCmp(String, Val, Val) [function]
   211	
   212	  // ==== shared list helpers =================================================
   213	  syntax Vals ::= appendVal(Vals, Val) [function, total]
   214	  rule appendVal(.Vals, V:Val)              => V , .Vals
   215	  rule appendVal((V0:Val, VS:Vals), V:Val)  => V0 , appendVal(VS, V)
   216	
   217	  syntax ValSeq ::= vals2valSeq(Vals) [function, total]
   218	  rule vals2valSeq(.Vals)            => .ValSeq
   219	  rule vals2valSeq((V:Val, VS:Vals)) => vCons(V, vals2valSeq(VS))
   220	
   221	  // ==== shared sequence length (len / summaries across many modules) ========
   222	  // (positional access valSeqAt/intSeqAt + normIdx live in subscript.k)
   223	  syntax Int ::= vsLen(ValSeq) [function, total]
   224	  rule vsLen(.ValSeq)                => 0
   225	  rule vsLen(vCons(_:Val, S:ValSeq)) => 1 +Int vsLen(S)
   226	
   227	  syntax Int ::= isLen(IntSeq) [function, total]
   228	  rule isLen(.IntSeq)                => 0
   229	  rule isLen(iCons(_:Int, S:IntSeq)) => 1 +Int isLen(S)
   230	
   231	  // in-bounds positional write (list subscript-assign); OOB leaves the seq unchanged
   232	  // (valid programs write in-bounds — mirrors valSeqAt's total-but-underspecified stance)
   233	  syntax ValSeq ::= setVSAt(ValSeq, Int, Val) [function, total]
   234	  rule setVSAt(.ValSeq, _:Int, _:Val)               => .ValSeq
   235	  rule setVSAt(vCons(_:Val, S:ValSeq), 0, V:Val)    => vCons(V, S)
   236	  rule setVSAt(vCons(W:Val, S:ValSeq), I:Int, V:Val) => vCons(W, setVSAt(S, I -Int 1, V))
   237	       requires I >Int 0
   238	  rule setVSAt(VS:ValSeq, I:Int, _:Val)             => VS
   239	       requires I <Int 0
   240	endmodule
     1	// reference/src/semantics/call.k — MPY-CALL
     2	// ONE call route for every callable: evaluate the callee to a VALUE (name lookup reaches
     3	// builtins at the root; a cooled Attribute is a bound method), evaluate the args (the shared
     4	// #evalArgs loop in core.k), then dispatch on the callee value:
     5	//   closureVal    -> bind params, push a frame (user function)
     6	//   boundMethodV  -> applyMethod
     7	//   builtinV      -> the #iterNext folds (sum/all/any/max/min) or applyBuiltin
     8	//   typeV         -> callable type objects: int(...) / str(...)
     9	
    10	module MPY-CALL
    11	  imports MPY-METHODS
    12	  imports MPY-BUILTINS
    13	  imports MPY-FUNCTIONS
    14	
    15	  // a cooled attribute is a bound method value
    16	  rule <k> Attribute(V:Val, M:String) => boundMethodV(V, M) ... </k>
    17	
    18	  // evaluate callee, then args ([owise]: problem-local Call interceptions beat this)
    19	  syntax KItem ::= #callee(Exprs)
    20	  rule <k> Call(Fe:Expr, ARGS:Exprs) => Fe ~> #callee(ARGS) ... </k> [owise]
    21	  rule <k> CV:Val ~> #callee(ARGS:Exprs) => #evalArgs(ARGS, .Vals, toCall(CV)) ... </k>
    22	
    23	  // ==== dispatch on the callee value ========================================
    24	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(OBJ:Val, M:String)), ACC:Vals) => applyMethod(OBJ, M, ACC) ... </k>
    25	
    26	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sum")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #sumAcc(OBJ, 0) ... </k>
    27	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("all")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #allAcc(OBJ)    ... </k>
    28	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("any")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #anyAcc(OBJ)    ... </k>
    29	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("max")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #maxAcc0(OBJ)   ... </k>
    30	  rule <k> #apply…1512 tokens truncated…ent scope; every other import is a no-op
    35	  rule <k> ImportFrom("math", NS:ParamNames) => #bindImports(NS) ... </k>
    36	  rule <k> ImportFrom(_:String, _:ParamNames) => .K ... </k> [owise]
    37	  syntax KItem ::= #bindImports(ParamNames)
    38	  rule <k> #bindImports(.ParamNames) => .K ... </k>
    39	  rule <k> #bindImports((N:String, NS:ParamNames)) => #bindImports(NS) ... </k>
    40	       <env> L:Int </env>
    41	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ N <- builtinV(N) ], _) ... </scopes>
    42	       requires N ==String "floor" orBool N ==String "ceil"
    43	  rule <k> #bindImports((N:String, NS:ParamNames)) => #bindImports(NS) ... </k>
    44	       requires notBool (N ==String "floor" orBool N ==String "ceil")
    45	
    46	  // ==== Expr statement: evaluate for effect, discard the value ===============
    47	  // (bare calls — mutator methods, docstrings; the WP0 statement-trivia rung)
    48	  rule <k> Expr(_:Val) => .K ... </k>
    49	
    50	  // ==== If (condition evaluated by strictness) ==============================
    51	  syntax KItem ::= #branch(Bool, Stmts, Stmts)
    52	  rule <k> If(C:Val, T:Stmts, E:Stmts) => #branch(truthy(C), T, E) ... </k>
    53	  rule <k> #branch(true,  T:Stmts, _:Stmts) => T ... </k>
    54	  rule <k> #branch(false, _:Stmts, E:Stmts) => E ... </k>
    55	
    56	  // ==== IfExp: ternary T if C else E ========================================
    57	  rule <k> IfExp(V:Val, T:Expr, _:Expr) => T ... </k>
    58	       requires truthy(V)
    59	  rule <k> IfExp(V:Val, _:Expr, E:Expr) => E ... </k>
    60	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    61	
    62	  // ==== For: one loop, in-cell continuation, over #iterNext =================
    63	  // (the iterable is evaluated once, by strictness; the protocol stays rewrites —
    64	  // circularities anchor on #loop and narrowing substitutes the structure)
    65	  syntax KItem ::= #loop(Val, Expr, Stmts) | #loopStep(Expr, Stmts)
    66	                 | #while(Expr, Stmts) | #whileCond(Expr, Stmts)
    67	                 | #loopLbl(K) | "#cont" | "#brk"
    68	
    69	  rule <k> For(T:Expr, OBJ:Val, B:Stmts) => #loop(OBJ, T, B) ... </k>
    70	
    71	  rule <k> #loop(IT:Iterable, T:Expr, B:Stmts) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #loopStep(T, B) ... </k>
    72	  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #loopStep(_:Expr, _:Stmts) => .K ... </k>
    73	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, REST:Iterable) ~> #loopStep(T:Expr, B:Stmts)
    74	        => #bindTgt(T, V) ~> B ~> #loopLbl(#loop(REST, T, B)) ... </k>
    75	
    76	  // ==== While ==============================================================
    77	  rule <k> While(C:Expr, B:Stmts) => #while(C, B) ... </k>
    78	  rule <k> #while(C:Expr, B:Stmts) => C ~> #whileCond(C, B) ... </k>
    79	  rule <k> V:Val ~> #whileCond(C:Expr, B:Stmts) => B ~> #loopLbl(#while(C, B)) ... </k>
    80	       requires truthy(V)
    81	  rule <k> V:Val ~> #whileCond(_C:Expr, _B:Stmts) => .K ... </k>
    82	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    83	
    84	  // ==== loop control (break / continue) =====================================
    85	  rule <k> #loopLbl(NEXT:K) => NEXT ... </k>
    86	  rule <k> Continue => #cont ... </k>
    87	  rule <k> Break => #brk ... </k>
    88	  rule <k> #cont ~> #loopLbl(NEXT:K) => NEXT ... </k>
    89	  rule <k> #cont ~> (_:KItem => .K) ... </k> [owise]
    90	  rule <k> #brk ~> #loopLbl(_:K) => .K ... </k>
    91	  rule <k> #brk ~> (_:KItem => .K) ... </k> [owise]
    92	
    93	  // ==== heap-object deref at the truthiness/iteration consumers ==============
    94	  // (priority(40) preempts the generic Val rules so truthy/#loop never see a ref)
    95	  rule <k> If(ref(H:Int), T:Stmts, E:Stmts) => If(V, T, E) ... </k>
    96	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    97	       [priority(40)]
    98	  rule <k> IfExp(ref(H:Int), T:Expr, E:Expr) => IfExp(V, T, E) ... </k>
    99	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
   100	       [priority(40)]
   101	  rule <k> ref(H:Int) ~> #whileCond(C:Expr, B:Stmts) => V ~> #whileCond(C, B) ... </k>
   102	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
   103	       [priority(40)]
   104	  // For derefs its iterable ONCE at loop start (iteration is over the snapshot;
   105	  // mutating the iterated list inside its own loop is outside the subset)
   106	  rule <k> For(T:Expr, ref(H:Int), B:Stmts) => For(T, V, B) ... </k>
   107	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
   108	       [priority(40)]
   109	endmodule
     1	// reference/src/semantics/iter.k — MPY-ITER
     2	// The iterator protocol, DECLARATION ONLY. Each iterable's #iterNext case lives in that
     3	// iterable's own module (list/tuple/str in their modules, rangeObj in range.k, zip in
     4	// builtins.k). Consumers (the for-loop, `x in _`, sum/all/any/max/min) import this.
     5	
     6	module MPY-ITER
     7	  imports MPY-CORE
     8	  syntax KItem ::= #iterNext(Iterable) | "#iterDone" | #iterYield(Val, Iterable)
     9	endmodule
     1	// reference/src/semantics/list.k — MPY-LIST
     2	
     3	module MPY-LIST
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	  imports MPY-ITER
     6	  imports MPY-OPERATORS
     7	
     8	  // ==== iteration (the iterator protocol's list case) =======================
     9	  rule <k> #iterNext(list(.ValSeq))                => #iterDone ... </k>
    10	  rule <k> #iterNext(list(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq))) => #iterYield(V, list(R)) ... </k>
    11	
    12	  // ==== ListExpr: [...] literal -> a fresh heap object =======================
    13	  syntax ApplyK ::= "toList"
    14	  rule <k> ListExpr(ES:Exprs) => #evalArgs(ES, .Vals, toList) ... </k>
    15	  rule <k> #applyK(toList, ACC:Vals) => #alloc(list(vals2valSeq(ACC))) ... </k>
    16	
    17	  // ==== list ops: + / == / != ===============================================
    18	  syntax ValSeq ::= valSeqConcat(ValSeq, ValSeq) [function, total]
    19	  rule valSeqConcat(.ValSeq, T:ValSeq)                => T
    20	  rule valSeqConcat(vCons(V:Val, S:ValSeq), T:ValSeq) => vCons(V, valSeqConcat(S, T))
    21	
    22	  // list + list constructs a NEW object (k-cell — it allocates; operands land here
    23	  // already deref'd). priority(45) beats the generic BinOp dispatch.
    24	  rule <k> BinOp("+", list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq)) => #alloc(list(valSeqConcat(A, B))) ... </k>
    25	       [priority(45)]
    26	
    27	  rule applyCmp("==", list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq)) => A ==K B
    28	  rule applyCmp("!=", list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq)) => notBool (A ==K B)
    29	
    30	  // ==== deep equality when elements are heap objects (list-of-lists) ========
    31	  // Python == is structural at every depth. Fires ONLY when a ref is present
    32	  // (the guard decides on concrete seqs); the plain ==K path above is unchanged.
    33	  syntax Bool ::= hasRefVS(ValSeq) [function, total]
    34	  rule hasRefVS(.ValSeq)                => false
    35	  rule hasRefVS(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq)) => isRefV(V) orBool hasRefVS(R)
    36	
    37	  syntax Bool ::= deepEqVS(ValSeq, ValSeq, Map) [function]
    38	                | deepEqV(Val, Val, Map)        [function]
    39	  rule deepEqVS(.ValSeq, .ValSeq, _:Map)                   => true
    40	  rule deepEqVS(.ValSeq, vCons(_:Val, _:ValSeq), _:Map)    => false
    41	  rule deepEqVS(vCons(_:Val, _:ValSeq), .ValSeq, _:Map)    => false
    42	  rule deepEqVS(vCons(A:Val, As:ValSeq), vCons(B:Val, Bs:ValSeq), HP:Map)
    43	    => deepEqV(A, B, HP) andBool deepEqVS(As, Bs, HP)
    44	
    45	  rule deepEqV(ref(H:Int), B:Val, HP:Map) => deepEqV({HP[H]}:>Val, B, HP)
    46	       requires H in_keys(HP)
    47	  rule deepEqV(A:Val, ref(H:Int), HP:Map) => deepEqV(A, {HP[H]}:>Val, HP)
    48	       requires notBool isRefV(A) andBool H in_keys(HP)
    49	  rule deepEqV(list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq), HP:Map) => deepEqVS(A, B, HP)
    50	  rule deepEqV(A:Val, B:Val, _:Map) => A ==K B [owise]
    51	
    52	  // ==== mutator: xs.append(v) — an in-place heap write ======================
    53	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(ref(H:Int), "append")), (V:Val, .Vals)) => noneV ... </k>
    54	       <heap> ... H |-> list(VS:ValSeq => valSeqConcat(VS, vCons(V, .ValSeq))) ... </heap>
    55	       [priority(40)]
    56	
    57	  // ==== `x in list` — a <k>-cell fold over #iterNext ========================
    58	  syntax KItem ::= #memberAcc(Val, Iterable) | #memberCont(Val) | "#notB"
    59	  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp("in",     list(VS:ValSeq))) => #memberAcc(LV, list(VS)) ... </k>
    60	  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp("not in", list(VS:ValSeq))) => #memberAcc(LV, list(VS)) ~> #notB ... </k>
    61	  rule <k> #memberAcc(V:Val, IT:Iterable) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #memberCont(V) ... </k>
    62	  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #memberCont(_V:Val) => false ... </k>
    63	  rule <k> #iterYield(E:Val, _:Iterable) ~> #memberCont(V:Val) => true ... </k>
    64	       requires E ==K V
    65	  rule <k> #iterYield(E:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #memberCont(V:Val) => #memberAcc(V, R) ... </k>
    66	       requires notBool (E ==K V)
    67	  rule <k> B:Bool ~> #notB => notBool B ... </k>
    68	endmodule
     1	// reference/src/semantics/subscript.k — MPY-SUBSCRIPT
     2	
     3	module MPY-SUBSCRIPT
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	
     6	  // ==== positional access + negative-index normalization (used only here) ===
     7	  // valSeqAt is [total]: in-bounds vCons access reduces as usual; on an OPAQUE sequence (e.g.
     8	  // a trusted sort's sortVS(VS)) or OOB it stays an abstract total value — so indexing the
     9	  // opaque sorted list is DEFINED (no undischarged #Ceil), matching the old semantics' total
    10	  // atK. K trusts the [total] annotation; valid programs index in-bounds.
    11	  syntax Val ::= valSeqAt(ValSeq, Int) [function, total]
    12	  rule valSeqAt(vCons(V:Val, _:ValSeq), 0)     => V
    13	  rule valSeqAt(vCons(_:Val, S:ValSeq), I:Int) => valSeqAt(S, I -Int 1)
    14	       requires I >Int 0
    15	
    16	  syntax Int ::= intSeqAt(IntSeq, Int) [function]
    17	  rule intSeqAt(iCons(C:Int, _:IntSeq), 0)     => C
    18	  rule intSeqAt(iCons(_:Int, S:IntSeq), I:Int) => intSeqAt(S, I -Int 1)
    19	       requires I >Int 0
    20	
    21	  syntax Int ::= normIdx(Int, Int) [function, total]
    22	  rule normIdx(I:Int, LEN:Int) => I +Int LEN requires I  <Int 0
    23	  rule normIdx(I:Int, _:Int)   => I          requires I >=Int 0
    24	
    25	  // ==== Subscript: indexing obj[i] (list / tuple / str) =====================
    26	  // contexts (not strict attrs): the Index slot's Slice alternative must never heat
    27	  context Subscript(HOLE, _)
    28	  context Subscript(_:Val, HOLE:Expr)
    29	
    30	  // heap-object deref (covers both the index and slice forms via the Index slot)
    31	  rule <k> Subscript(ref(H:Int), IX:Index) => Subscript(V, IX) ... </k>
    32	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    33	       [priority(40)]
    34	
    35	  rule <k> Subscript(OBJ:Val, I:Int) => applyIndex(OBJ, I) ... </k>
    36	
    37	  syntax Val ::= applyIndex(Val, Int) [function]
    38	  rule applyIndex(list(VS:ValSeq),  I:Int) => valSeqAt(VS, normIdx(I, vsLen(VS)))
    39	  rule applyIndex(tuple(VS:ValSeq), I:Int) => valSeqAt(VS, normIdx(I, vsLen(VS)))
    40	  rule applyIndex(str(IS:IntSeq),   I:Int)
    41	    => str(iCons(intSeqAt(IS, normIdx(I, isLen(IS))), .IntSeq))
    42	
    43	  // ==== Slice: obj[lo:hi:step] (list / str) — CPython slice.indices ==========
    44	  syntax KItem ::= #evalB(Bound) | "#toSome"
    45	                 | #slLo(Val, Bound, Bound)
    46	                 | #slHi(Val, OptInt, Bound)
    47	                 | #slStep(Val, OptInt, OptInt)
    48	
    49	  syntax OptInt ::= "noB" | someB(Int)
    50	  rule <k> #evalB(NoBound)  => noB ... </k>
    51	  rule <k> #evalB(E:Expr)   => E ~> #toSome ... </k>
    52	  rule <k> I:Int ~> #toSome => someB(I) ... </k>
    53	
    54	  rule <k> Subscript(OBJ:Val, Slice(LO:Bound, HI:Bound, ST:Bound)) => #evalB(LO) ~> #slLo(OBJ, HI, ST) ... </k>
    55	  rule <k> LO:OptInt ~> #slLo(OBJ:Val, HI:Bound, ST:Bound)   => #evalB(HI) ~> #slHi(OBJ, LO, ST) ... </k>
    56	  rule <k> HI:OptInt ~> #slHi(OBJ:Val, LO:OptInt, ST:Bound)  => #evalB(ST) ~> #slStep(OBJ, LO, HI) ... </k>
    57	  // a list slice constructs a NEW object; a str slice stays a value
    58	  rule <k> ST:OptInt ~> #slStep(list(VS:ValSeq), LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt)
    59	        => #alloc(doSlice(list(VS), LO, HI, ST)) ... </k>
    60	       [priority(45)]
    61	  rule <k> ST:OptInt ~> #slStep(OBJ:Val, LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt) => doSlice(OBJ, LO, HI, ST) ... </k>
    62	
    63	  syntax Val ::= doSlice(Val, OptInt, OptInt, OptInt) [function]
    64	  rule doSlice(list(VS:ValSeq), LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt, ST:OptInt)
    65	    => list(buildVS(VS, slStart(LO, ST, vsLen(VS)), slStop(HI, ST, vsLen(VS)), slStep(ST)))
    66	  rule doSlice(tuple(VS:ValSeq), LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt, ST:OptInt)
    67	    => tuple(buildVS(VS, slStart(LO, ST, vsLen(VS)), slStop(HI, ST, vsLen(VS)), slStep(ST)))
    68	  rule doSlice(str(IS:IntSeq), LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt, ST:OptInt)
    69	    => str(buildIS(IS, slStart(LO, ST, isLen(IS)), slStop(HI, ST, isLen(IS)), slStep(ST)))
    70	
    71	  // ==== slice.indices: step / start / stop / clamp ==========================
    72	  syntax Int ::= slStep(OptInt) [function, total]
    73	  rule slStep(noB)          => 1
    74	  rule slStep(someB(S:Int)) => S
    75	
    76	  syntax Int ::= slStart(OptInt, OptInt, Int) [function]
    77	  rule slStart(noB,          ST:OptInt, _LEN:Int) => 0
    78	       requires slStep(ST) >Int 0
    79	  rule slStart(noB,          ST:OptInt, LEN:Int)  => LEN -Int 1
    80	       requires slStep(ST) <Int 0
    81	  rule slStart(someB(I:Int), ST:OptInt, LEN:Int)  => slAdjust(I, LEN, slStep(ST))
    82	
    83	  syntax Int ::= slStop(OptInt, OptInt, Int) [function]
    84	  rule slStop(noB,          ST:OptInt, LEN:Int)  => LEN
    85	       requires slStep(ST) >Int 0
    86	  rule slStop(noB,          ST:OptInt, _LEN:Int) => -1
    87	       requires slStep(ST) <Int 0
    88	  rule slStop(someB(I:Int), ST:OptInt, LEN:Int)  => slAdjust(I, LEN, slStep(ST))
    89	
    90	  syntax Int ::= slAdjust(Int, Int, Int) [function, total]
    91	  rule slAdjust(I:Int, LEN:Int, STEP:Int) => clampLo(I +Int LEN, STEP)
    92	       requires I  <Int 0
    93	  rule slAdjust(I:Int, LEN:Int, STEP:Int) => clampHi(I, LEN, STEP)
    94	       requires I >=Int 0
    95	
    96	  syntax Int ::= clampLo(Int, Int) [function, total]
    97	  rule clampLo(J:Int, _STEP:Int) => J
    98	       requires J >=Int 0
    99	  rule clampLo(J:Int, STEP:Int)  => #if STEP <Int 0 #then -1 #else 0 #fi
   100	       requires J <Int 0
   101	
   102	  syntax Int ::= clampHi(Int, Int, Int) [function, total]
   103	  rule clampHi(I:Int, LEN:Int, _STEP:Int) => I
   104	       requires I  <Int LEN
   105	  rule clampHi(I:Int, LEN:Int, STEP:Int)  => #if STEP <Int 0 #then LEN -Int 1 #else LEN #fi
   106	       requires I >=Int LEN
   107	
   108	  // ==== build the strided sub-sequence (indices in range by construction) ====

Removing them makes the entry proof fail at the symbolic `slAdjust/buildVS` residual, while fixed-semantics ground witnesses agree with their equations. I found no false-conclusion witness for an unsound local rule, so I’m recording this as a validation gap, not fabricating an unsoundness finding.

+# Independent adversarial review: 122-add-elements
+
+## Executive finding
+
+The candidate reconstructs successfully and its K entry claim genuinely
+executes the constructor body in the submitted `solution.mpy`. The claim is
+result-constraining and rejects both a body mutation and a false
+postcondition. However, the submitted program and the proved summary implement
+the wrong criterion on a material part of the stated integer domain.
+
+The trusted canonical implementation at `/reference/canonical.py:20` includes
+an element exactly when `len(str(elem)) <= 2`. The candidate at
+`/candidate/solution.py:4` instead includes it when `abs(elem) < 100`. These
+criteria differ on every negative two-digit integer. A minimal satisfying
+source-contract witness is `arr = [-99], k = 1`: the canonical result is `0`,
+while both the candidate and its proved K summary return `-99`.
+
+This is not a bounded-domain issue, a timeout, or an infrastructure
+uncertainty. It is a deterministic intended-domain implementation/specification
+failure. Under the benchmark decision boundary, the candidate is not a
+legitimate proof of the requested HumanEval contract.
+
+## 1. Input and provenance integrity
+

+`SUPPLIED_SEMANTICS`, and `/reference/reference-semantics` is present as
+required. No mode/mount contradiction exists.
+

+
+Generation records claimed `KPROVE_PASSED` and 10,000 differential successes,

+## 2. Program fidelity and candidate-versus-canonical checks
+
+### Contract
+
+From `/reference/prompt.py:2-15`, `arr` is a non-empty list of integers with
+`1 <= len(arr) <= 100`, and `k` is an integer with
+`1 <= k <= len(arr)`. The required result is the sum, among the first `k`
+elements, of those having at most two digits. The trusted executable
+interpretation is `/reference/canonical.py:20`:
+
+```python
+sum(elem for elem in arr[:k] if len(str(elem)) <= 2)
+```
+
+Thus `-9` qualifies because `str(-9)` has length two, while `-10` through
+`-99` do not because the minus sign makes their string length three.
+
+The candidate instead executes:
+
+```python
+if abs(element) < 100:
+    total += element
+```
+
+That agrees for non-negative integers and for one-digit negatives, but
+incorrectly includes all negative two-digit integers.
+
+### Trusted translation
+
+From a fresh scratch copy, I ran:
+
+```text
+python3 py2mpy.py solution.py > regenerated-solution.mpy
+cmp -s regenerated-solution.mpy solution.mpy
+```
+
+Both files have SHA-256
+`7b5c94215b395cce642414d4e864a3643404201eabef94b6355fa8b8f264a779`;
+`cmp` and the logged command exited 0. Therefore the submitted `solution.mpy`
+is exactly the trusted translation of the submitted `solution.py`.
+See `evidence/stage2-translation-byte-identity.log`.
+
+### Independent differential test
+
+`evidence/stage2_differential.py` imports the two Python entry points from
+separate files and uses the trusted canonical function as the oracle. It covers:
+
+- the documented example;
+- minimum and maximum array lengths;
+- `k = 1` and `k = len(arr)`;
+- the branch boundaries
+  `-1000, -100, -99, -10, -9, -1, 0, 9, 10, 99, 100, 1000`;
+- 5,000 deterministic generated valid inputs with seed `12220260726`;
+- an empty-array/zero-`k` diagnostic clearly labeled outside the contract.
+
+All 5,009 intended-domain inputs are preserved in
+`evidence/stage2-differential-inputs.json` (SHA-256
+`69ec553a78314a967e188cd7dff9e5cfaf43a8065f4cd3f859e6d14b6d9dde58`).
+The script exited 1 after finding 3,759 mismatches. The smallest is:
+
+```text
+arr=[-99], k=1, canonical=0, candidate=-99
+```
+
+The empty outside-contract diagnostic returned 0 from both implementations;
+it does not cure the intended-domain failures. Exact results are in
+`evidence/stage2-differential.log`.
+
+Stage 2 result: failed program fidelity to the trusted HumanEval contract.
+
+## 3. Clean proof reconstruction
+
+All execution occurred in `/tmp/audit-work/122-add-elements-audit`. I copied
+only source artifacts and the trusted supplied semantics. No candidate-provided
+compiled definition or cache was copied or used. The live tools report K
+version `v7.1.293`.
+
+The following fresh commands were run:
+
+| Purpose | Command | Exit/result |
+|---|---|---|
+| Concrete definition | `kompile reference-semantics/semantics.k --backend llvm --main-module MPY-KRUN --syntax-module MPY-SYNTAX --output-definition audit-runtime-kompiled` | 0 |
+| Load submitted module | `krun solution.mpy --definition audit-runtime-kompiled` | 0; `.K`, `NoExc`, exit code 0; closure body visible in scope 0 |

+| All original positive claims | `kprove spec.k --definition audit-verification-kompiled --spec-module ADD-ELEMENTS-SPEC` | 0 and `#Top` |
+| Labeled loop claim alone | `kprove spec-labeled.k --definition audit-verification-kompiled --spec-module ADD-ELEMENTS-SPEC-LABELED --claims ADD-ELEMENTS-SPEC-LABELED.loop-invariant` | 0 and `#Top` |
+
+The exact bounded outputs are in `evidence/stage3-kompile-llvm.log`,
+`stage3-krun-solution.log`, `stage3-krun-candidate-tests.log`,
+`stage3-kompile-haskell.log`, `stage3-kprove-all.log`, and
+`stage3-kprove-loop-only.log`.
+
+The original proof command proves the full two-claim set, including the entry
+claim. As a diagnostic, I selected the entry label alone; removing the loop
+circularity made symbolic execution continue unboundedly, so I manually
+interrupted that non-authoritative filtered run with status 130 after about 85
+seconds. This is recorded in `evidence/stage3-kprove-entry-only.log` and is not
+used as a candidate defect or as a substitute for the successful original
+all-claims run.
+
+The candidate smoke test passes, but its fourth assertion expects `-99` for an
+input beginning with `-99`. It therefore confirms the wrong implementation,
+not the trusted contract.
+
+Stage 3 result: clean verification succeeded under the submitted theory.
+
+## 4. Adequacy and real-program pinning
+
+### Claims in plain language
+
+The helper claim at `/candidate/spec.k:9-49` says: given an active loop over an
+arbitrary non-empty `ValSeq` of integers, an integer accumulator, a local loop
+frame, and no global shadowing of `abs`, execution consumes the loop and leaves
+`total` equal to `qualifyingSumAcc` of the old accumulator and the whole input
+sequence. The final loop-variable value is existential; the return-relevant
+accumulator is not.
+
+The entry claim at `/candidate/spec.k:54-108` says: choose integer sequences
+`HEAD :: PREFIX` and `SUFFIX`, with total length at most 100. Call a closure
+whose parameters and body are written explicitly, using
+`arr = (HEAD :: PREFIX) ++ SUFFIX` and
+`k = len(HEAD :: PREFIX)`, from the normal module/builtin configuration. If the
+call terminates, its result is exactly
+`qualifyingSumAcc(0, HEAD :: PREFIX)`. A non-empty prefix gives `k >= 1`, the
+suffix decomposition gives `k <= len(arr)`, and the length guard covers the
+source upper bound.
+
+### Mechanical program identity
+
+`evidence/stage4_pinning_and_witnesses.py` mechanically extracts the
+`FuncDef` from `solution.mpy` and the `closureVal` from the entry claim. After
+only list-syntax normalization (`.Stmts` terminators and whitespace), the two
+constructor bodies have the same SHA-256:
+
+```text
+99b61d6b8450346419a018e80927eacf8cd9a198231b735cf4ef1842dec7751d
+```
+
+The parameter lists are both `["arr", "k"]`, and the closure parent is module
+scope 0. The supplied `FuncDef` rule creates exactly this closure in scope 0,
+so directly starting the call is a semantically inert normalization of module
+loading, not a substituted body. The body still executes assignment, slicing,
+iteration, builtin lookup/call, comparison, conditional addition, and return
+through fixed semantics.
+
+The destination is not a free variable or tautology. It fixes the returned
+integer summary. Heap and allocation cells are existential at the end because
+list slicing allocates and the source contract observes only the return value;
+control, stack, return state, exception state, and exit code are pinned.
+
+### Satisfiable witnesses and substitution
+
+For `arr=[111,21,3,4000,5], k=3`, take
+`HEAD=111`, `PREFIX=[21,3]`, `SUFFIX=[4000,5]`. Every entry precondition holds,
+and the formal summary, candidate, and canonical all produce 24.
+
+For `arr=[-99], k=1`, take `HEAD=-99` and both sequences empty. Every entry
+precondition also holds. The formal result and candidate are `-99`, while the
+canonical result is `0`. This directly locates the adequacy failure inside the

+A helper-claim witness with `GLOBALS={}`, `ACC=5`, `V=21`, and
+`VS=[3,4000]` satisfies all loop preconditions and has claimed final total 29.

+`evidence/stage4-pinning-and-witnesses.log`.

+
+`spec-body-sensitivity.k` changes the threshold in the executed closure term
+from 100 to 99 and keeps the original result obligation for ground input
+`[99]`. It builds against the fresh proof definition. `kprove` exits 1 with
+`WarnStuckClaimState`; the residual has result 0 while the destination requires

+actually executed by the claim, not merely an external source file.

+that program/formal result is inadequate for the trusted source contract.
+
+## 5. Rule-by-rule static soundness review
+
+### Exhaustive inventory
+
+`evidence/stage5_inventory.py` produced the exhaustive machine-readable
+inventory `evidence/stage5-rule-inventory.json` and the human-readable,
+rule-by-rule table `evidence/stage5-rule-inventory.md`. It includes every
+mounted supplied-semantics K file plus `verification.k` and `spec.k`.
+
+Inventory totals are:
+
+- 1,060 outer K sentences;
+- 709 rules (695 fixed supplied-semantics rules and 14 proof-local rules);
+- 230 syntax declarations;
+- 148 declarations carrying `function`, `total`, or a functional attribute;
+- 45 priority rules;
+- 8 simplification rules;

+Every declaration, rule, attribute, file/module, line range, normalized hash,
+and disposition is recorded. The independent canonical simplifier inventory
+in `evidence/stage5-canonical-simplification-inventory.log` confirms exactly
+the eight proof-local simplifiers.

+The supplied tree contains intentionally opaque fixed symbols for features such
+as symbolic float operations, sorting, and MD5:
+`sortVS`, `sortKeyVS`, `intFloatDiv`, `divII`, `floatMod`, `floatLt`, `absF`,
+`subF`, `divF`, `addF`, `mulF`, `powF`, `gtF`, `eqF`, `decStrToF`,
+`divFloatIntV`, `intToF`, `truncF`, `roundF`, `roundFN`, `sqrtF`, and

+
+### Used fixed-semantics path
+
+The used construct map is explicit in the inventory. On the material path:
+
+- the configuration supplies module scope 0, builtin scope -1, heap, stack,
+  return, exception, and exit cells;
+- `FuncDef` creates `closureVal(params, body, 0)`;
+- call routing evaluates the callee and arguments left-to-right, allocates a
+  fresh frame, binds parameters, executes the body, and restores caller
+  control on return;
+- assignment and augmented assignment update the active scope; integer

+- list slicing evaluates bounds in order, normalizes the positive step,
+  constructs the slice via `buildVS`, and allocates the new list;
+- the `For` rule evaluates the iterable once, uses `#iterNext`, binds each loop

+- `abs` resolves through the builtin scope and its fixed integer rule;
+- integer comparison selects the correct branch; `Return` sets the return cell,
